claims.text: The proposed initial material is a homogeneous, fine-grained, single-phase equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, or a similar compositionally complex alloy.
The proposed initial HEA has a uniform elemental distribution.
The proposed initial HEA has high intrinsic toughness.
Cyclic loading or elevated-temperature exposure can induce grain-boundary-localized atomic reordering or elemental redistribution in an initially single-phase HEA.
The induced grain-boundary changes take the form of short-range order or subtle partitioning rather than a conventional brittle grain-boundary precipitate.
The combination of sluggish diffusion and high local strain fields promotes limited atomic reordering during extended cyclic or elevated-temperature exposure.
Atomic reordering or redistribution preferentially occurs at stress concentrations such as grain boundaries.
Short-range ordering or incipient segregation at grain boundaries reduces grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion lowers the effective fracture toughness.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion causes a transition from ductile transgranular fracture to brittle intergranular fracture.
Exposure at approximately 600–700 °C and/or repeated service-like cyclic loading is sufficient to activate the proposed grain-boundary rearrangement.
Exposed specimens will show detectable grain-boundary chemistry or short-range-order changes by APT or high-resolution TEM relative to a room-temperature static control.
Exposed specimens will exhibit more intergranular fracture than the initial baseline.
Exposed specimens will have lower fracture toughness or lower tensile/bending ductility than the initial baseline.
The proposed mechanism operates below the thresholds for full-scale recrystallization and bulk precipitation.
The mechanism is expected to apply to grain sizes and compositions typical of engineering HEAs used in demanding environments.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as produced by equilibrium processing, whereas the falsification experiment specifies as-cast specimens. As-cast material may not reproduce the asserted equilibrium-processed homogeneous baseline.
